— https://nitter.net/ianmSC/status/2

The Athletic has lost roughly $500 million since its founding. It’s just a modern day online version of $1 CDs in the 1980’s — sign up for a $1 for a year! — & then most people forget they subscribed and & don’t realize they are still being charged. Except you got CDs at least!
I sucked a guy’s dick — either legitimately or metaphorically — and now know eight minutes before the team announces a trade via email release isn’t really that important of a job.

Real sports media reporting value, which used to exist and now mostly doesn’t, is news that would otherwise not exist but for a reporter’s hard work. That’s very valuable & almost nonexistent. All trade & contract news will be announced by teams soon after the “news” breaks.

There should be a deeper conversation about sports media reporting — “scoops” that would become news no matter what — trades & contract news for instance — isn’t actually that important or even really reporting. It’s just access trading.

Just a reminder as the Russini saga plays out, @TheAthletic has lost hundreds of millions of dollars since it was founded, yet @nytimes paid over $500 million for the company and now uses it to (mostly) make far left wing sports content the larger sports fan market detests.
This isn’t a morals judgement, by the way, just a basic job analysis. If Vrabel were gay and banging the back up quarterback, it probably wouldn’t help him analyze the QB situation.
